help.name: Network troubleshooting
help.desc: Slow, dropping or dead internet and WiFi.

issues.title: The internet is crawling
issues.why: Usually too many people streaming or a big download hogging the line. Bad weather or something blocking the Starlink dish does it too.
issues.fix: Pause big downloads and video, then restart the router. Wait two minutes before judging it.
steps: Ask whether anyone is streaming, uploading or downloading something large, and pause it.
Restart the router: off for 30 seconds, then on, and wait two minutes.
Run a speed test and compare it with the speed you pay for.
If it is slow for everyone at all hours, the line itself needs checking by the provider.

issues.title: No internet at all
issues.why: The router or Starlink lost power, a cable got kicked loose, or the provider has an outage. Sometimes the bill simply ran out.
issues.fix: Check the router lights and the power cable. Try another device. If every device is down, it is the line and not your computer.
steps: Look at the router lights. No lights means a power problem. A red or blinking internet light means the line is down.
Check that every cable is pushed in fully, including the one from the wall or dish.
Test a second device. If only one device is offline, the fault is that device.
Confirm the internet bill is paid, then call the provider with the light pattern you see.

issues.title: WiFi connects, then keeps dropping
issues.why: You are far from the router, there are thick walls in between, or the router is overloaded and overheating.
issues.fix: Move closer, forget the network and join again, and give the router some air.
steps: Stand next to the router. If it is stable there, distance or walls are the cause.
Forget the network on your device and reconnect with the password.
Feel the router. If it is hot, move it into open air and restart it.
Count connected devices. Cheap routers struggle beyond about 15 to 20.

issues.title: One device cannot connect while others can
issues.why: That device has a wrong saved password, a stuck network setting or its WiFi switched off. Occasionally the router has blocked it.
issues.fix: Forget the network on that device and join again, then restart the device.
steps: Check that WiFi is on and aeroplane mode is off on that device.
Forget the network and reconnect, typing the password carefully.
Restart the device, then try it on a phone hotspot to prove its WiFi works.
If it works on the hotspot but not the office WiFi, the router may be blocking it.

issues.title: The internet slows at the same time every day
issues.why: Scheduled backups or updates, a busy period in the office, or your provider's line being congested at peak hours.
issues.fix: Note the times it happens for three days. Check whether a backup or update runs then.
steps: Write down the times it slows for a few days.
Check whether backups, updates or cloud sync are scheduled at those times.
Run a speed test during a slow period and again when it is fine.
Send both results to the agent. A big gap at peak hours points to the provider.

issues.title: A network point or cable is dead
issues.why: A damaged or unplugged cable, a faulty wall socket or a dead port on the switch.
issues.fix: Try the same device and cable on another wall point, then another cable on the same point.
steps: Move the same device and cable to a point you know works.
Then try a cable you know works on the dead point.
Look at the switch: no light on that port means the cable run or the port has failed.
Label the dead point so nobody else wastes time on it.

issues.title: Calls and video keep breaking up
issues.why: Unstable connection rather than slow speed: weak WiFi, a failing cable or an overloaded router dropping data.
issues.fix: Plug the computer in by cable for a call. If it is perfect on cable, the WiFi is the problem.
steps: Join a call using a network cable. Perfect on cable means WiFi is the cause.
Close cloud sync, downloads and other video while on calls.
Move nearer the router or use the 5 GHz WiFi band if your router offers it.
If cable calls also break up, the line or router needs a proper test.

help.name: Router and WiFi setup
help.desc: New routers, Starlink, WiFi coverage and passwords.

issues.title: Set up a new router
issues.why: A new office, a new internet provider or an old router that has reached the end of its life.
issues.fix: Have the provider's account details and the box the router came in ready. Do not plug in a second router alongside the old one yet.
steps: Unplug the old router fully before the new one is connected.
Connect the new router to the provider's line and power it on.
Sign in to its settings page using the address and login on its sticker.
Set a new admin password, a WiFi name and a strong WiFi password before anyone connects.

issues.title: Set up Starlink for the office
issues.why: Moving to satellite internet, or adding it as a backup line.
issues.fix: Pick a spot with a clear view of the sky and no trees or roof edges above it. The Starlink app has an obstruction check.
steps: Use the Starlink app's obstruction check to choose the dish position.
Mount the dish firmly. Wind moving it causes dropouts.
Run the cable so it is not pinched by doors or windows.
Decide whether Starlink is your main line or a backup. That changes how it connects to your router.

issues.title: WiFi does not reach some rooms
issues.why: Distance, concrete walls and metal roofing weaken the signal. One router is rarely enough for a whole building.
issues.fix: Move the router to a central, raised spot away from walls and metal cabinets.
steps: Walk around with a phone and note where the signal bars drop.
Move the router to a central, raised position and test again.
If dead spots remain, you need extra access points, ideally wired back to the router.
Avoid cheap plug-in repeaters for office work. They halve the speed.

issues.title: Create a guest WiFi
issues.why: Visitors and customers need internet, but should not be on the same network as your work computers.
issues.fix: Check the router's settings page for a Guest network switch. Many routers have one built in.
steps: Sign in to the router's settings page.
Turn on the Guest network and give it a different name and password.
Switch on the option that isolates guests from the main network, if there is one.
Share only the guest password with visitors from now on.

issues.title: Change the WiFi name or password
issues.why: Too many people know the password, a staff member left, or it is still the default on the sticker.
issues.fix: Sign in to the router's settings page, open Wireless and change it there. Every device will need the new password.
steps: Sign in to the router's settings page with the admin login.
Open the Wireless or WiFi section and enter the new name or password.
Use at least 12 characters mixing words and numbers.
Reconnect each work device with the new password and do not write it on the wall.

issues.title: I am locked out of the router settings
issues.why: The admin password was changed and forgotten, or was never written down.
issues.fix: Look for the default login on the router's sticker. Avoid the reset button for now, because it wipes the internet settings too.
steps: Try the default login printed on the router's sticker.
Ask whoever installed it, or your provider, whether they set the password.
A factory reset is the last resort: it erases the internet settings, so have the provider's details first.
After regaining access, set a new admin password and store it safely.

help.name: Network configuration
help.desc: Addresses, sharing, separate networks and cabling.

issues.title: Two devices are fighting over the same address
issues.why: Two devices were given the same IP address, usually because one was set by hand. You see 'IP address conflict' warnings.
issues.fix: Restart both devices so the router hands out fresh addresses.
steps: Restart both devices so each asks the router for a fresh address.
If the warning returns, one of them has an address typed in by hand.
Set that device back to obtain its address automatically.
Devices that must keep one address should have it reserved in the router instead.

issues.title: Give a printer or server a fixed address
issues.why: Printers and servers that change address keep 'disappearing' from everyone's computers.
issues.fix: Note the device's current IP address from its network settings page so the agent can reserve it.
steps: Find the device's current address in its network settings.
Sign in to the router and open the DHCP or address reservation page.
Reserve that address for the device so it never changes.
Reconnect any computers that lost the printer and they will keep it this time.

issues.title: Share a printer or folder across the office
issues.why: Staff need the same printer or files, and emailing documents around has become unworkable.
issues.fix: Make sure the computers are on the same WiFi or network, not the guest one.
steps: Confirm every computer is on the same office network.
For a printer, add it by its network address on each computer.
For folders, share from one always-on computer or a storage box, with named users.
Avoid 'Everyone' permissions. Give access per person or per team.

issues.title: Separate staff, guest and CCTV networks
issues.why: Everything on one flat network means one infected device can reach the accounts computer and the cameras.
issues.fix: List what you have: how many computers, cameras, printers and guest users. That decides the design.
steps: List the groups to keep apart: staff, guests, cameras, tills, servers.
Check your router and switches support VLANs. Basic home routers often do not.
The agent builds a separate network for each group and sets which may talk to which.
Each WiFi name is then tied to its own group.

issues.title: Reach an office system from outside
issues.why: You want to view cameras, a server or the accounts system from home or another branch.
issues.fix: Do not open ports yourself by guesswork. An open port is a door for attackers as well as for you.
steps: Say exactly what you need to reach and from where.
A VPN is the safer route for most cases and is usually what the agent will recommend.
If a port must be opened, it is limited to specific addresses and a strong password.
Test from mobile data, never from inside the office.

issues.title: Network cabling and new points
issues.why: A new office, more desks, or WiFi that will never be stable enough for the work.
issues.fix: Sketch the floor with where desks, printers and the router will sit, and count the points you need.
steps: Mark on a sketch where each point is needed.
The agent measures cable runs and chooses the cable grade and switch size.
Cables are run, terminated, labelled at both ends and tested.
You get a simple map of which point goes to which switch port.

issues.title: Some websites will not open
issues.why: A DNS problem: the service that turns website names into addresses is failing or blocked.
issues.fix: Try the same site on mobile data. If it opens there, the fault is on your office network.
steps: Try the site on mobile data to see whether it is only your network.
Restart the router, which often clears a stuck DNS setting.
On one computer, switch DNS to a public service to test.
If that fixes it, the agent changes DNS on the router for everyone.

help.name: Firewall and VPN
help.desc: Firewalls, website blocking and VPN for remote work.

issues.title: Set up a firewall for the office
issues.why: The office has grown, handles customer data or payments, or has already had a scare.
issues.fix: Count your users and devices and note your internet speed. Those three numbers size the firewall.
steps: Agree what must be protected: accounts system, customer data, payment devices.
The agent recommends a firewall sized for your users and internet speed.
It is installed between the internet line and your network, with safe default rules.
You receive the admin login, a summary of the rules and who to call for changes.

issues.title: Block unwanted or risky websites
issues.why: Staff time lost to streaming and betting sites, or malware arriving through unsafe downloads.
issues.fix: Decide the categories you want blocked and who, if anyone, should be exempt.
steps: Agree the categories to block and any exceptions.
Filtering is switched on at the router or firewall so it covers every device.
Test with a blocked site and an allowed one.
Review the list after two weeks, since legitimate sites are sometimes caught.

issues.title: A program is being blocked by the firewall
issues.why: A new program or an update needs a connection the firewall does not recognise, so it is stopped.
issues.fix: Note the exact program name and the error message, and when it last worked.
steps: Note the program, the error and when it last worked.
The agent checks the firewall log to see exactly what was blocked.
A narrow rule is added for that program only, not a general opening.
You test, and the rule is recorded with the reason it exists.

issues.title: Staff need a VPN to work from home
issues.why: People need office files and systems from home or on the road, safely.
issues.fix: List who needs remote access and which systems. Not everyone needs everything.
steps: List the people and the systems they need from home.
The agent sets up the VPN on the firewall or router with a login per person.
Each laptop or phone gets the VPN app and two-step verification.
Access is removed the day someone leaves.

issues.title: Link two branches securely
issues.why: Two offices need to share files, printers or one accounts system as if they were in one building.
issues.fix: Note the internet provider and router model at each branch.
steps: The agent checks the router or firewall at each branch can build a tunnel.
A secure link is configured between the two sites.
Rules decide which systems each branch can reach.
Both ends are tested for speed and for recovery after a power cut.

issues.title: Review my firewall rules
issues.why: Rules pile up over the years. Old openings left for former suppliers are a common way in.
issues.fix: Find out who set the firewall up and whether anyone still has the admin login.
steps: The agent exports the current rules and port openings.
Each rule is checked: who needs it, and is it still used.
Unused and over-wide rules are removed or tightened.
You get a short report of what changed and why.

issues.title: The shared drive or NAS is unreachable
issues.why: The storage box lost power or network, its address changed, or a disk inside has failed.
issues.fix: Check its power and network lights, then restart your own computer before anything else.
steps: Check the storage box has power and its network light is on.
Restart your computer and try again by its network address.
If one person is locked out, it is a permissions issue. If everyone is, it is the box or network.
A clicking sound or red disk light means stop and raise a ticket at once.

issues.title: Set up automatic backups
issues.why: Backups done by hand get forgotten, usually just before the day they are needed.
issues.fix: Decide which folders matter most and how much work you could afford to lose: a day, or a week.
steps: Pick the folders and systems that must be backed up.
Choose where copies go: a storage box in the office and one copy off-site or in the cloud.
The agent schedules the backup to run automatically, usually at night.
A test restore is done so you know it works.

issues.title: The server will not start
issues.why: A failed disk or power supply, a bad update, or damage from a power surge.
issues.fix: Do not keep forcing it on. Note any beeps, lights or messages on the screen.
steps: Check the power cable, socket and UPS first.
Note any error on the screen, beeps or coloured lights.
Do not reinstall or reset anything, as that can destroy data.
The agent diagnoses on-site and recovers data before any repair.

help.name: CCTV and office devices
help.desc: Cameras, phone viewing and attendance devices.

issues.title: Cameras are offline
issues.why: Power to the camera or recorder is off, a cable is damaged, or the recorder's disk is full or failed.
issues.fix: Check the recorder is on and its cables are firm. See whether one camera or all of them are down.
steps: Check whether one camera or all are down.
One camera: check its cable and power at both ends.
All cameras: check the recorder's power and its disk status in the menu.
Note when recording stopped, in case footage from that period is needed.

issues.title: I cannot view cameras on my phone
issues.why: The recorder lost its internet connection, the app login changed, or remote viewing was never set up properly.
issues.fix: Check you can see the cameras on the recorder's own screen first. If yes, only remote viewing is broken.
steps: Confirm the cameras show on the recorder's own screen.
Check the recorder's network cable and that the internet is working.
Sign out and back in to the viewing app with the correct account.
If it still fails, the agent re-links the recorder to the app.

issues.title: The attendance or biometric device is not syncing
issues.why: It has dropped off the network, its address changed, or the software on the computer was updated.
issues.fix: Restart the device and check the network cable or WiFi icon on its screen.
steps: Restart the device and check it shows a network connection.
Confirm the computer with the attendance software is on the same network.
Check the device's address has not changed in its network menu.
The agent re-links it and reserves its address so it stays put.

help.name: Website, domain and business email
help.desc: Website down, domains and company email.

issues.title: Our website is down
issues.why: Hosting or the domain has expired, the hosting company has an outage, or a bad update broke the site.
issues.fix: Open the site on mobile data to confirm it is down for everyone and not only in your office.
steps: Test on mobile data to confirm it is down for everyone.
Check for renewal or suspension emails from the hosting company.
Sign in to the hosting account, if you have the login, and look for notices.
The agent traces whether the fault is the domain, the hosting or the site itself.

issues.title: Our domain has expired or is about to
issues.why: Renewal reminders went to an old email address or the card on file failed.
issues.fix: Find out who registered it and where. Renew quickly: expired domains can be bought by someone else.
steps: Find the registrar from old invoices or emails.
Sign in and renew straight away, for more than one year if you can.
Turn on auto-renew and update the contact email.
If it has already lapsed, the agent helps with recovery, which can cost more the longer it is left.

issues.title: Set up business email on our own domain
issues.why: Staff are using personal Gmail or Yahoo addresses, which looks unprofessional and leaves with them.
issues.fix: Decide the addresses you need, for example info@ and accounts@, and who will own each.
steps: Choose the provider, for example Google Workspace or Microsoft 365.
The agent verifies your domain with the provider.
Mail records are changed so email arrives in the new mailboxes.
Each person gets an account, a strong password and two-step verification.

help.name: Email and accounts
help.desc: Passwords, locked accounts and missing email.

issues.title: I forgot my password
issues.why: It happens after a holiday, a forced password change or one too many similar passwords.
issues.fix: Use the Forgot password link on the sign-in page. If two-step verification is blocking you, raise a ticket.
steps: Open the sign-in page and choose Forgot password.
Follow the code sent to your recovery phone or email.
Choose a new password you have not used before.
Update it on your phone and tablet straight away.

issues.title: My account is locked
issues.why: Too many wrong password attempts, often from an old phone still trying the previous password.
issues.fix: Wait 15 minutes, then try once carefully. Update the password on your phone and tablet too.
steps: Stop trying for 15 minutes so the lock can clear.
Check Caps Lock and type the password slowly once.
Update the password on every device that checks your mail.
If it locks again quickly, an old device or someone else is trying it.

issues.title: Emails are not sending or arriving
issues.why: A full mailbox, an attachment that is too large, or a wrong address. Missing mail often lands in spam.
issues.fix: Check Spam and the Outbox, shrink the attachment, and confirm the address letter by letter.
steps: Look in Spam for missing mail and in Outbox for stuck mail.
Check your mailbox is not full and delete large old messages.
Send large files as a shared link instead of an attachment.
Ask the other person to check the address they used.

issues.title: I need a new email or shared mailbox
issues.why: A new starter, a new project or a role that needs a team address.
issues.fix: Raise a ticket with the name, the role and the manager who approved it.
steps: Decide the address name and who will use it.
Get your manager's approval.
The agent creates it and sets who can read and send.
You sign in and change the temporary password.

issues.title: My computer is painfully slow
issues.why: Too many programs opening at startup, a nearly full disk, or weeks without a restart. Sometimes an update is working in the background.
issues.fix: Restart it properly, close browser tabs you are not using, and clear your Downloads folder.
steps: Restart, do not only close the lid.
Close programs and browser tabs you are not using.
Free up disk space: empty the bin and clear Downloads.
If it is slow from the moment it starts, too many programs launch at startup.

issues.title: It will not turn on
issues.why: A flat battery, a loose or faulty charger, or a power surge. Laptops also sulk after a hard knock.
issues.fix: Try a different socket and charger. Hold the power button for 15 seconds, release, then press once.
steps: Try another socket and, if possible, another charger.
Hold the power button for 15 seconds, release, then press once.
Unplug everything attached and try again.
A charging light with no screen points to the display, not the power.

issues.title: Blue screen or sudden restarts
issues.why: A faulty driver after an update, overheating from blocked vents, or failing memory or disk.
issues.fix: Write down or photograph the error code, let the machine cool, and raise a ticket with the photo.
steps: Photograph the error screen, including the code.
Recall what changed: a new device, program or update.
Let the machine cool, then restart.
If it happens more than once, stop using it for important work until it is checked.

issues.title: The laptop is hot and the fan is loud
issues.why: Dust in the vents, working on a bed or sofa, or one program stuck using all the power.
issues.fix: Put it on a hard flat surface, close heavy programs and restart.
steps: Move it to a hard, flat surface so the vents are clear.
Close heavy programs and restart.
Listen for the fan. No fan sound with high heat needs a technician.
Dust build-up is cleaned by opening the machine, which is a job for the agent.

help.name: Printers and scanners
help.desc: Printing, paper jams, faint prints and scanning.

issues.title: Nothing comes out when I print
issues.why: The printer is offline, the job went to a different printer, or an earlier job is stuck in the queue.
issues.fix: Check you picked the right printer, cancel all waiting jobs, then switch the printer off and on.
steps: Check the printer is on, has paper and shows no error.
Confirm you chose the right printer in the print window.
Open the print queue and cancel every waiting job.
Turn the printer off and on, then print one test page.

issues.title: Paper jam
issues.why: Damp or crumpled paper, an overfilled tray, or worn rollers. Humid days make it worse.
issues.fix: Switch it off, pull the paper out gently in the direction it travels, and reload with a fresh, fanned stack.
steps: Switch the printer off.
Open the covers and pull the paper gently in the direction it travels.
Check for torn scraps left inside.
Reload with a fresh, fanned stack and do not overfill the tray.

issues.title: Prints are faint or streaky
issues.why: Toner or ink is running low, or the cartridge needs a shake or a clean.
issues.fix: Take the toner out, rock it side to side and refit. Run the cleaning cycle from the printer menu.
steps: Remove the toner or ink cartridge and rock it gently side to side.
Refit it firmly until it clicks.
Run the cleaning cycle from the printer's menu.
If prints are still faint, the cartridge needs replacing.

issues.title: Scan to email stopped working
issues.why: The email password the printer uses was changed, or the address book entry is wrong.
issues.fix: Scan to a USB stick for now and raise a ticket so IT can update the printer's email settings.
steps: Scan to a USB stick so work can continue.
Check whether the email password the printer uses was changed recently.
The agent updates the printer's mail settings.
A test scan is sent to confirm.

issues.title: I need a program installed
issues.why: A new task, a new role or a file type your computer cannot open yet.
issues.fix: Raise a ticket naming the program and what you need it for. Please do not download cracked copies.
steps: Name the program and what you need it for.
Get approval if it costs money.
The agent checks it is safe and properly licensed.
It is installed remotely and tested with you.

issues.title: The ERP or accounts system shows an error
issues.why: A lost connection, a session that timed out, or missing permission for that screen.
issues.fix: Refresh, sign out and back in, and screenshot the exact error if it returns.
steps: Refresh the page and try again.
Sign out and back in.
Screenshot the exact error and note what you were doing.
Check whether colleagues see the same thing. If so, it is the system, not you.

issues.title: A program keeps freezing or crashing
issues.why: It needs an update, the file is very large, or the computer is short of memory.
issues.fix: Save your work, close other programs, restart the app and install pending updates.
steps: Save your work if you can.
Close other programs to free memory.
Install pending updates for that program.
If one file causes it, the file may be damaged or too large.

issues.title: It says my licence has expired
issues.why: The subscription ran out or was moved to another user.
issues.fix: Raise a ticket with the program name and the exact message. Keep working in the web version if there is one.
steps: Note the program and the exact message.
Check whether a renewal email arrived.
Use the web version, if there is one, to keep working.
The agent confirms the subscription and reassigns the licence.

help.name: Phones and M-Pesa devices
help.desc: Work phones, till phones and SIM problems.

issues.title: The work phone will not sync email
issues.why: The password was changed on the computer but not the phone, or mobile data is off or finished.
issues.fix: Open the mail app, re-enter the new password and check your data bundle.
steps: Open the mail app's account settings.
Enter the new password.
Check mobile data or WiFi is on and working.
Remove and re-add the account if it still will not sync.

issues.title: The till phone is not receiving M-Pesa messages
issues.why: A full message inbox, weak signal, or the SIM has shifted in the tray. Network delays also happen at peak hours.
issues.fix: Delete old messages, restart the phone and check the balance from the M-Pesa menu instead of waiting for SMS.
steps: Delete old messages to free inbox space.
Restart the phone and check signal bars.
Check the balance from the M-Pesa menu instead of waiting for the SMS.
Take the SIM out, wipe it gently and refit it.

issues.title: The SIM suddenly shows no service
issues.why: A damaged SIM, an unpaid line or, in the worst case, a fraudulent SIM swap.
issues.fix: Treat it as urgent. Call your mobile provider from another phone straight away and raise an urgent ticket.
steps: Restart the phone and check aeroplane mode is off.
Try the SIM in another phone.
If it shows no service there too, call the provider from another line immediately.
Ask them directly whether a SIM swap was done. If yes, treat it as fraud.

help.name: Security worries
help.desc: Suspicious messages, viruses and lost devices.

issues.title: I got a suspicious email or message
issues.why: Scammers send thousands of these, hoping one person clicks. Your address may be on a leaked list.
issues.fix: Do not click, reply or open attachments. Forward it to IT and delete it.
steps: Do not click links, open attachments or reply.
Check the sender's real address, not only the display name.
Forward it to IT, then delete it.
Warn colleagues if it looks aimed at your company.

issues.title: I think I clicked a bad link
issues.why: The message looked real. That is exactly what the people who write them are good at.
issues.fix: Disconnect from WiFi, change your password from another device and raise an urgent ticket. Nobody will be cross.
steps: Disconnect that device from WiFi or unplug its cable.
From a different device, change your password.
Tell IT at once, with the time and what you clicked.
Do not use the affected device until it has been checked.

issues.title: Antivirus found something, or pop-ups everywhere
issues.why: A dodgy download, a cracked program or an infected flash disk.
issues.fix: Leave the antivirus to finish, do not plug in any USB sticks, and raise a ticket.
steps: Let the antivirus finish and note the name of what it found.
Do not plug in USB sticks or open downloads.
Restart only when the scan says it is safe.
The agent checks whether anything else was affected.

issues.title: I lost my laptop or phone
issues.why: Left in a matatu, a taxi or a meeting room, or stolen.
issues.fix: Raise an urgent ticket now so IT can lock it and reset your passwords. Tell us where and when you last had it.
steps: Report it immediately with where and when you last had it.
IT locks or wipes the device remotely if that is set up.
Change your email and system passwords.
For a phone, call the mobile provider to block the SIM.

help.name: New starters and leavers
help.desc: Accounts and access for joiners and leavers.

issues.title: Someone new is joining
issues.why: A new hire needs accounts, a device and access before day one.
issues.fix: Raise a ticket at least three working days ahead with name, role, start date and the systems they need.
steps: Send the name, role, start date and manager at least three days ahead.
List the systems and folders they need.
The agent creates accounts and prepares a device.
On day one they sign in, change passwords and set up two-step verification.

issues.title: Someone is leaving
issues.why: Access left open after a person leaves is a risk to them and to the business.
issues.fix: Raise a ticket with their last working day so accounts are closed and equipment collected.
steps: Tell IT the last working day as soon as it is known.
List what they had: laptop, phone, access cards.
Accounts are disabled at the end of the last day.
Their mail and files are handed to the manager.

issues.title: I need access to a system or folder
issues.why: A new responsibility, a project move or cover for a colleague.
issues.fix: Raise a ticket naming the system and the manager who approved it.
steps: Name the system or folder and why access is needed.
Get the owner's or manager's approval.
The agent grants the minimum needed.
Say when it is no longer needed so it can be removed.

help.name: Equipment requests
help.desc: New or replacement equipment and repairs.

issues.title: I need a new mouse, keyboard or headset
issues.why: Wear and tear, a spill, or one that simply walked away.
issues.fix: Raise a ticket saying what you need and whether the old one is broken.
steps: Say what you need and whether the old one is broken.
Hand in the faulty item if asked.
The agent issues a replacement from stock or orders one.
It is recorded against your name.

issues.title: My screen is cracked or flickering
issues.why: A drop, pressure in a bag, a loose cable or a tired display.
issues.fix: Check the cable is firmly in at both ends. If the laptop screen itself is cracked, raise a ticket with a photo.
steps: Check the cable at both ends, or try another cable.
Connect another screen to see whether the laptop itself is fine.
Photograph the damage.
The agent quotes for repair or replacement. Parts are charged separately.

issues.title: I need a laptop or replacement
issues.why: A new role, an ageing machine or one beyond repair.
issues.fix: Raise a ticket with your manager's approval and what you use the machine for.
steps: Describe the work you do and the programs you use.
Get your manager's approval.
The agent recommends a specification and price.
Your files and settings are moved across from the old machine.

help.name: Files and backup
help.desc: Deleted files, shared folders and full storage.

issues.title: I deleted a file by mistake
issues.why: A slip of the finger, or a tidy-up that went one folder too far.
issues.fix: Check the Recycle Bin or Drive Bin first. Deleted files usually wait there for about 30 days.
steps: Open the Recycle Bin or Drive Bin.
Search for the file name, then restore it.
If it is not there, check with whoever shares the folder.
Older deletions may need restoring from backup, which the agent can do.

issues.title: I cannot open a shared folder
issues.why: You were never added, the folder moved, or your sign-in expired.
issues.fix: Ask the folder owner to share it again, or raise a ticket with the folder name.
steps: Check you are signed in with your work account.
Ask the folder owner to share it with you again.
Try opening it from the link they send.
If the folder was moved, the agent finds the new location.

issues.title: My storage is full
issues.why: Videos, duplicate downloads and years of attachments add up quietly.
issues.fix: Empty the bin, clear Downloads and move old projects to the shared archive.
steps: Empty the bin.
Sort files by size and delete or move the largest.
Clear Downloads and duplicate videos.
Move old projects to the shared archive.

help.name: Meetings and video calls
help.desc: Sound, projectors and choppy video calls.

issues.title: Nobody can hear me on the call
issues.why: The wrong microphone is selected, you are muted, or the browser has no microphone permission.
issues.fix: Check the mute button, then pick the right microphone in the call settings.
steps: Check the mute button in the call and on the headset.
Open the call's audio settings and choose the right microphone.
Allow microphone access when the browser asks.
Rejoin the call, or restart the computer if it still fails.

issues.title: The projector or TV shows nothing
issues.why: The wrong input is selected, a loose HDMI cable, or the laptop is not set to share its screen.
issues.fix: Reseat the cable, pick the right HDMI input and press Windows + P to choose Duplicate.
steps: Check both ends of the HDMI cable.
Choose the correct HDMI input on the projector or TV.
Press Windows + P and choose Duplicate.
Try another cable or laptop to find which part is at fault.

issues.title: Video calls keep freezing
issues.why: A weak connection, many people on the same WiFi, or too many programs open.
issues.fix: Turn your camera off, move closer to the router and close other apps.
steps: Turn your camera off to save bandwidth.
Move closer to the router or plug in a cable.
Close other programs and browser tabs.
Ask others on the WiFi to pause heavy downloads during the call.

help.name: Power and UPS
help.desc: A beeping UPS and equipment after blackouts.

issues.title: The UPS is beeping
issues.why: It is running on battery because mains power dropped, or its battery is near the end of its life.
issues.fix: Save your work now. If mains power is fine and it still beeps, raise a ticket for a battery check.
steps: Save your work straight away.
Check whether mains power is actually off.
If mains is fine and it still beeps, note the pattern and any warning light.
The battery usually needs replacing every two to three years.

issues.title: Equipment died after a blackout
issues.why: A power surge when electricity came back, or a tripped extension.
issues.fix: Check the socket and extension switch. Do not keep forcing the power button. Raise a ticket.
steps: Check the socket with another device.
Check the extension switch and any tripped breaker.
Unplug the equipment and leave it for a few minutes before one more try.
Do not keep forcing it. Surge damage needs a technician.

bands.what: Quick fix by chat or phone

bands.what: On-site investigation, hardware fault or security incident

band_advice: Fix it yourself with the quick fix. Still stuck? Raise a ticket.
Try the quick fix. If it fails, an agent can fix it remotely.
An agent can fix this remotely through a ticket.
Needs hands-on work: book an agent visit or use a nearby shop.
Serious fault: stop using it and raise an urgent ticket, or visit a nearby shop.

qs.action: Change the WiFi password from the default
qs.text: Is your office WiFi protected by a strong password that is different from the one printed on the router?
qs.why: Default router passwords are easy to look up. Anyone in range can join your network.

qs.action: Change the router or Starlink admin login
qs.text: Has the admin login for your router or Starlink kit been changed from the factory default?
qs.why: Whoever controls the router can watch or redirect all your traffic.

qs.action: Set up a separate guest WiFi
qs.text: Do visitors and customers use a separate guest WiFi from the one your work devices use?
qs.why: A visitor's infected phone should never sit on the same network as your accounts computer.

qs.text: Is a firewall switched on at your internet connection?
qs.why: A firewall blocks unwanted connections from the internet before they reach your devices.

qs.action: Give remote staff a secure connection
qs.text: Do staff use a VPN or other secure connection when working from home, a cyber cafe or public WiFi?
qs.why: Public WiFi can be read by others. A VPN keeps work traffic private.

qs.text: Is your network split so guest, staff, server and CCTV traffic are kept apart?
qs.why: Segments stop one infected device from reaching everything else.

qs.text: Does someone review network logs or alerts for unusual activity?
qs.why: Most break-ins leave traces days before the damage. Someone has to be looking.

qs.action: Turn on two-step verification for email
qs.text: Do all staff use two-step verification on work email?
qs.why: Also called 2FA or MFA. A stolen password alone is then not enough to get in.

qs.action: Remove leavers' accounts the same day
qs.text: Are accounts disabled on the day a staff member leaves?
qs.why: Old accounts are a favourite way back in, for outsiders and unhappy former staff.

qs.action: Give every person their own login
qs.text: Does each staff member have their own login, with no shared accounts?
qs.why: With shared logins you cannot tell who did what, or remove one person's access.

qs.action: Use unique passwords or a password manager
qs.text: Do staff use a password manager or a different password for each system?
qs.why: One reused password leaked from another site can open every system you have.

qs.text: Are admin rights limited to the few people who need them?
qs.why: Malware runs with the rights of whoever opened it. Fewer admins means less damage.

qs.text: Do you use single sign-on or central identity management?
qs.why: One place to add, change and remove access is far easier to keep right.

qs.text: Are access rights reviewed at least every 6 months?
qs.why: People change roles and keep old access unless someone checks.

qs.text: Can staff spot phishing emails and scam messages on WhatsApp and SMS?
qs.why: Most attacks start with a message that tricks a person, not a technical break-in.

qs.action: Verify changes to payment details by phone
qs.text: Do you confirm any request to change a supplier's bank or paybill details by calling a number you already know?
qs.why: Fraudsters send convincing emails asking you to pay a "new" account.

qs.text: Have staff had cybersecurity training in the last 12 months?
qs.why: Scams change every year. Training keeps people current.

qs.action: Name a person to report to
qs.text: Do staff know who to tell when they see something suspicious?
qs.why: A quick report can stop an attack. Silence lets it spread.

qs.action: Brief new staff in week one
qs.text: Are new staff briefed on security rules in their first week?
qs.why: New starters are targeted because they do not yet know what normal looks like.

qs.text: Do you run simulated phishing tests?
qs.why: Practice with safe fake emails shows who needs more help.

qs.text: Are computers and phones set to install updates automatically?
qs.why: Updates close holes that attackers already know how to use.

qs.text: Is antivirus protection active on every computer?
qs.why: It catches most common malware before it runs.

qs.text: Is all your software properly licensed, with no cracked copies?
qs.why: Cracked software is a leading source of malware and gets no security updates.

qs.text: Do all work phones and laptops lock with a PIN, password or fingerprint?
qs.why: An unlocked lost phone hands over email, files and payment apps.

qs.text: Are laptops and phones encrypted?
qs.why: Encryption keeps data unreadable if the device is stolen.

qs.text: Do you keep a list of company devices and who holds each one?
qs.why: You cannot protect or recover what you do not know you own.

qs.text: Is the use of personal USB sticks controlled or scanned?
qs.why: Flash disks carry malware between home, cyber cafes and the office.

qs.action: Set up remote lock and wipe
qs.text: Can you remotely lock or wipe a lost device?
qs.why: Device management lets you protect data after a device is gone.

qs.text: Are important files backed up automatically at least once a week?
qs.why: Ransomware, theft or a failed disk can wipe out years of records.

qs.action: Keep one backup offsite or offline
qs.text: Is one backup copy kept away from the office or offline?
qs.why: Fire, theft or ransomware can take the backup too if it sits next to the original.

qs.text: Have you tested restoring from a backup in the last 6 months?
qs.why: A backup you have never restored is only a hope.

qs.text: Are your accounting, ERP or point-of-sale records included in the backup?
qs.why: These are the records the business and KRA will ask for first.

qs.action: Prepare for power and internet outages
qs.text: Can you keep working through a power or internet outage?
qs.why: A UPS and a second connection keep sales and records running.

qs.text: Do you have a written recovery plan with target times?
qs.why: It tells everyone what to restore first and how long it should take.

qs.action: Restrict who knows the M-Pesa PIN
qs.text: Is your M-Pesa PIN known only to authorised people and never shared by call, SMS or WhatsApp?
qs.why: Nobody genuine will ever ask for your PIN, including callers who say they are from Safaricom.

qs.action: Confirm payments on your own line
qs.text: Do staff confirm each payment on your own till, app or statement before releasing goods?
qs.why: Fake confirmation SMS and edited screenshots are a common way to steal stock.

qs.text: Do staff know not to send money back when a caller claims a payment was sent by mistake?
qs.why: In this scam the "mistaken" payment was never real, or is reversed again afterwards.

qs.action: Protect the business line from SIM swap
qs.text: Have you asked your mobile provider about SIM swap protection for the business line?
qs.why: A fraudulent SIM swap moves your number, and your M-Pesa, to a criminal's phone.

qs.text: Are M-Pesa records checked against sales every day or week?
qs.why: Regular checks expose missing money and insider fraud early.

qs.action: Assign the payment phone to a named person
qs.text: Is the phone holding the business line locked and kept by a named person?
qs.why: A shared, unlocked payment phone makes theft easy and impossible to trace.

qs.action: Separate who starts and who approves payments
qs.text: Does one person start a large payment or withdrawal and a different person approve it?
qs.why: Two people make both mistakes and fraud much harder.

qs.text: Are till or paybill withdrawals limited to approved numbers or your business bank account?
qs.why: It stops funds being moved to a personal line.

qs.action: Give each portal operator their own login
qs.text: Does each operator on the M-Pesa business portal have their own login and role?
qs.why: Named operators give you an audit trail and let you remove one person cleanly.

qs.text: If you use the M-Pesa (Daraja) APIs, are keys stored securely, rotated and callbacks validated?
qs.why: Leaked API keys or unchecked callbacks let attackers fake or redirect payments.

qs.action: Register with the ODPC if required
qs.text: Are you registered with the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner where the law requires it?
qs.why: Kenya's Data Protection Act requires many organisations to register. Check whether yours is one.

qs.text: Are ID copies, payroll and customer lists locked away or limited to those who need them?
qs.why: Personal data is what criminals sell and what the law holds you responsible for.

qs.action: List the personal data you hold
qs.text: Do you know what personal data you hold on customers and staff?
qs.why: Names, ID numbers, phone numbers and M-Pesa records all count.

qs.action: Tell customers how you use their data
qs.text: Do you tell customers how their data is used and get consent where needed?
qs.why: People have a legal right to know. A short notice is usually enough.

qs.text: Do you shred paper records and wipe old devices before disposal?
qs.why: Old phones, disks and files in the bin leak data.

qs.action: Add data terms to supplier contracts
qs.text: Do contracts with suppliers who handle your data include data protection terms?
qs.why: You stay responsible for data even when a supplier holds it.

qs.text: Have you appointed a data protection officer or a named responsible person?
qs.why: Someone must own compliance and be the contact for the regulator.

qs.action: Assess new systems for privacy risk
qs.text: Do you carry out data protection impact assessments for new systems?
qs.why: It is required for high-risk processing and catches problems before launch.

qs.text: Do you have a written list of what to do and who to call if you are hacked or defrauded?
qs.why: In a crisis nobody thinks clearly. A simple list saves hours.

qs.text: Do you know how to report fraud to your bank or Safaricom, the police, the national KE-CIRT/CC and the ODPC?
qs.why: A personal data breach must be reported to the ODPC within 72 hours.

qs.action: Make lost devices reportable at once
qs.text: Do staff know how to report a lost or stolen device immediately?
qs.why: The first hour is when you can still lock accounts and SIMs.

qs.text: Do you keep a record of past incidents and what you changed afterwards?
qs.why: The same trick tends to be tried again.

qs.text: Have you practised an incident drill in the last year?
qs.why: A drill shows the gaps in the plan while nothing is at stake.

qs.action: Arrange cyber insurance or a reserve
qs.text: Do you have cyber insurance or money set aside for an incident?
qs.why: Recovery, legal advice and downtime cost money quickly.

qs.text: Is a senior manager or board member accountable for cybersecurity?
qs.why: Without an owner at the top, security loses every budget discussion.

qs.text: Is there a written information security policy that is reviewed every year?
qs.why: It sets the rules everyone else is measured against.

qs.action: Add cyber risks to the risk register
qs.text: Are cyber risks reviewed in your regular risk register?
qs.why: It keeps security in front of management alongside other business risks.

qs.text: Do you check the security of key suppliers and cloud providers before signing?
qs.why: Attackers often come in through a weaker supplier.

qs.text: Do you have independent security testing or an audit at least once a year?
qs.why: Outsiders find what the team that built it cannot see.

qs.text: Do you follow a recognised standard such as ISO 27001 or your sector regulator's guidance?
qs.why: A standard gives structure and evidence for customers and regulators.
